item.title: Wake Forest baseball coach Tom Walter placed on leave
item.description: Wake Forest has placed longtime baseball coach Tom Walter on leave, the university confirmed.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Wake Forest has placed longtime baseball coach Tom Walter on leave, the university confirmed. The school issued a statement Saturday after Wake Forest-centered site Demon Deacons Digest reported the news. No reason for the move has been disclosed. "Wake Forest baseball head coach Tom Walter is on leave effective October 14, 2026," spokesperson Ryan Madden told the outlet. "Additional information will be shared when it becomes appropriate. In accordance with University policy Wake Forest Athletics will have no further comment at this time." Eric Niesen, an assistant coach on the pitching side, currently is in charge of the program, with an assist from administrator Craig Zakrzewski. Before returning to his alma mater as a coach before the 2026 season, Niesen served as director of pitching for the Houston Astros. Walter began as the Demon Deacons' head coach in June 2009. The program made a fifth consecutive appearance in the NCAA Tournament in 2026 and reached the Men's College World Series in 2023. Chase Burns, Nick Kurtz, Gavin Sheets and Rhett Lowder are among the current major leaguers to have played for Walter. Walter was in the news in June 2025 after he appeared to utter a homophobic slur as his team lost to Tennessee in the NCAA Knoxville Regional. Video of the incident spread, and Walter apologized the next day. Athletic director John Currie called the conduct "disappointing" in a public rebuke. Walter has 536 career wins at Wake Forest. He owns a career record of 964-738-1 that includes his years as head coach at George Washington (1997-2004) and New Orleans (2005-09). He became the seventh coach to lead three programs to the NCAA Tournament at the Division I level. --Field Level Media

item.title: Report: Saints QB Tyler Shough playing with broken bones in left hand
item.description: New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough will once again be under center on Sunday against the New York Giants while playing with multiple broken bones in his non-throwing hand, ESPN reported.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough will once again be under center on Sunday against the New York Giants while playing with multiple broken bones in his non-throwing hand, ESPN reported. The Saints have listed Shough on the injury report with a hand injury, but the specifics have not been revealed by the team. He has continued to play through the injury that reportedly occurred in the Saints' 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons on Oct. 5. Shough has played with his ring and pinky fingers taped together while wearing a protective glove. It has not impacted his ability to pass the ball and he has completed handoffs on running plays with his right throwing hand. The injury is expected to take multiple months to fully heal, according to the report, with New Orleans set to go on its bye week after playing the Pittsburgh Steelers next Sunday in Paris. Shough, 27, has completed 66.8% of his passes for 1,299 yards and nine touchdowns with five interceptions as the Saints carried a 1-4 record into Sunday's game against the Giants. In two NFL seasons, the Saints' 2025 second-round draft pick has completed 67.3% of his passes for 3,683 yards, 19 touchdowns and 11 interceptions in 16 games, while New Orleans has gone 6-8 in his 14 starts. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brighton's patience pays off as Huerzeler helps Seagulls soar
item.description: Eight months after some Brighton & Hove Albion fans called for Fabian Huerzeler to be sacked after a home defeat by Crystal Palace, the young manager has the Seagulls soaring in third place in the Premier League after Sunday's 5-0 rout of the same opponents.
item.dc:creator: Rohith Nair
item.content:encoded: Eight months after some Brighton & Hove Albion fans called for Fabian Huerzeler to be sacked after a home defeat by Crystal Palace, the young manager has the Seagulls soaring in third place in the Premier League after Sunday's 5-0 rout of the same opponents. The 33-year-old, the youngest manager in the English top flight, watched his side demolish rivals Palace in a game capped by [USN:L4N464024 TEXT:"Diego Gomez's spectacular halfway-line strike"] that sent the home fans into raptures. It was a far cry from February's 1-0 defeat in the "M23 Derby" that left Brighton languishing in 14th place as some of the club's fans chanted "You're getting sacked in the morning." Brighton, however, refused to push the panic button and retained their faith in Huerzeler, who eventually guided the south-coast club to an eighth-placed finish. Chairman Tony Bloom [USN:L1N41K15A TEXT:"rewarded Huerzeler with a contract extension"] until 2029 and the club are reaping the benefits of the trust placed in the young German. LEAGUE-LEADING 23 GOALS With Sunday's 5-0 victory, Brighton sit five points behind leaders Manchester City with a league-leading 23 goals in seven games, five clean sheets and a goal difference of plus 18, six better than City's. "A few months ago (after losing to Palace) we were in a different place and I said I'd keep pushing to get another opportunity to beat them, so I'm happy we did it today," Huerzeler told Sky Sports. "It's not a one-man show, so I credit my players and my staff. Hopefully everyone enjoyed it." While Erling Haaland has scored eight of City's goals to move clear in the Golden Boot race, Brighton have already had 11 different scorers. "If you look, they're shared around a lot which is a massive help. We've got everyone chipping in and helping out the team," Brighton defender Lewis Dunk told BBC Radio. "If you look at our clean sheets, I think it's the most we've ever had at this part of the season, so we're buzzing with that as well." RELENTLESS PRESSING Brighton's success in the new campaign has been built on relentless pressing, a hallmark of last month's commanding 3-0 victory over champions Arsenal that left coach [USN:L6N45B053 TEXT:"Mikel Arteta searching for answers"] after his side's first defeat of the season. Pascal Gross's successful return has provided another major boost. The 35-year-old, who previously spent seven seasons at Brighton, rejoined the club earlier this year in search of regular first-team football. Gross is their joint-top scorer with three goals while the German also leads the team with four assists. It was his free kick that forced an own goal in the fourth minute that opened the floodgates against Palace. Dunk refused to entertain talk of a title challenge so early in the season, while Huerzeler was equally determined to keep expectations in check. "To me, the most important thing is the things we can improve... It's good to celebrate the win, but understand there is still space for improvement, especially for individual players," he said. "We have to keep going. We can't be satisfied. We have to keep pushing, stay humble and understand why we are successful at the moment to keep pushing at that level."

item.title: Trump says Washington golf course renovation to start in November, despite judge's order
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that his administration would begin renovation work next month on a historic Washington golf course that a federal judge had ordered could not proceed without prior court notification.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that his administration would begin renovation work next month on a historic Washington golf course that a federal judge had ordered could not proceed without prior court notification. The renovation work, which Trump earlier this year had said [USN:L1N43005N TEXT:"would begin in September"], has become the subject of a lawsuit over environmental and historic preservation concerns. Trump said in a post on Truth Social that work on the East Potomac Golf Links would begin on November 15 and that it would reopen in about 15 months. The renovation is among [USN:L6N41H110 TEXT:"a number of projects"] Trump is pursuing to reshape the White House and other Washington landmarks. US District Judge Ana Reyes ruled earlier this year that the government must give notice before any substantive construction work on the golf course could proceed, and last week [USN:L1N45Y0L4 TEXT:"issued an order"] halting the removal of trees at the site, which she called "inexcusable." The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment on whether Trump's announcement on Sunday would conflict with Reyes' directives. The DC Preservation League brought a lawsuit in February to halt the administration's takeover of the golf course, alleging that it would violate environmental laws and "irreparably destroy a priceless piece of American history." In an October 9 court filing, the Trump administration had asked Reyes to dismiss the litigation, saying it was premature because the "proposed project remains at an early and conceptual stage." The following day, however, the government removed about 500 trees from the site, which it said would improve safety at the park and restore its original design, and was part of a 2019 plan that predates Trump's ambitions for the course. Reyes ordered a halt to the removals. On Friday, the government filed a motion to disqualify Reyes and move the case to another district judge, saying her actions had shown "deep-seated and unequivocal antipathy toward the Trump Administration," according to court records.

item.title: McLaren to sell five F1 cars, all driven by champions and one by Brad Pitt
item.description: McLaren are selling five fully-functioning Formula One cars driven by champions, including Lewis Hamilton and the late Brazilian Ayrton Senna, with one also tested by Hollywood actor Brad Pitt.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: McLaren are selling five fully-functioning Formula One cars driven by champions, including Lewis Hamilton and the late Brazilian Ayrton Senna, with one also tested by Hollywood actor Brad Pitt. The cars, to be sold through high-end dealer Tom Hartley Jr. and expected to raise tens of millions of dollars, will be prepared by the reigning constructors' champions for their next owners. Hartley Jr. also sold the collection of [USN:L3N3PQ0Q7 TEXT:"former F1 supremo Bernie Ecclestone"] and 20 road cars belonging to the late McLaren co-owner [USN:L4N3UJ12T TEXT:"Mansour Ojjeh."] "We have decided to part with these iconic McLaren Formula One cars because we feel that having them simply sitting in storage is a disservice to what they represent," McLaren Racing CEO Zak Brown said in a statement on Sunday. "These cars were built to be driven and raced, and we want to see them being used and enjoyed. We believe that is the best way to keep our history alive and our heritage business active." PITT DROVE ONE AFTER FILMING F1 MOVIE The five span 32 years of McLaren history, starting with two MP4/6A cars (chassis numbers 04 and 07 with Honda V12 engines) raced by Austrian Gerhard Berger and tested by Senna during the 1991 title-winning campaign. Chassis 04 finished second in a one-two at the San Marino Grand Prix with the McLarens lapping the entire field. Chassis 07 came second at McLaren's home British Grand Prix. Both have been in McLaren's possession ever since. A 2012 McLaren MP4/27A (chassis 01) raced by 2009 world champion Jenson Button and tested by seven-times world champion Hamilton is also for sale. Two cars raced exclusively by reigning champion Lando Norris in 2021 and 2023 complete the group. The 2021 McLaren MCL35M took Norris to the podium in Imola, Monaco and Monza while the 2023 MCL37A-03 won successive races in Singapore and Japan and was tested post-season by a roster of drivers including Norris's teammate Oscar Piastri and Mick Schumacher, son of F1 great Michael. The 2023 McLaren was driven by Pitt in a private test at Austin's Circuit of the Americas in June last year in connection with his starring role in "F1 the Movie" and is the most modern F1 car offered for sale to a private owner. Pitt reportedly took it up to a speed of 197mph (317kph). "It is incredibly rare for a collector to have the opportunity to acquire race-driven Grand Prix cars directly from the manufacturer and team that built and campaigned them, and that makes this a very special offering," said Hartley. "These five cars will be offered individually and there is no time pressure whatsoever. Our priority, and McLaren’s, is to find the right homes for them." Although no prices were given, they are expected to range from 5 million pounds ($6.7 million) to as much as 10 million. A McLaren MP4-25A raced by Hamilton to victory in Turkey in 2010 sold for 4.8 million pounds in 2021 while a winning 2001 Ferrari raced by Michael Schumacher fetched $7.5 million in New York in 2017.

item.title: Flávio e Lula se enfrentam no primeiro debate; apoiadores ocupam as ruas
item.description: Brasileiros foram às ruas neste domingo em manifestações a favor e contra seus candidatos à Presidência, enquanto o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro se preparavam para seu primeiro debate televisionado, a uma semana do fim da campanha.
item.dc:creator: Brendan O'Boyle, Sebastian Recondio, Luis Nova
item.content:encoded: Brasileiros foram às ruas neste domingo em manifestações a favor e contra seus candidatos à Presidência, enquanto o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro se preparavam para seu primeiro debate televisionado, a uma semana do fim da campanha. Multidões pró-Bolsonaro, vestindo as cores nacionais do Brasil -- amarelo, verde e azul --, lotaram a Avenida Paulista, em São Paulo, onde o candidato discursou para os apoiadores. Apoiadores de Lula, vestidos de vermelho, cor simbólica do Partido dos Trabalhadores, lotaram a praça dos prédios do governo em Brasília, enquanto estudantes que apoiam o presidente protestaram contra Bolsonaro no Rio de Janeiro. As pesquisas mostram uma [USN:S0N45N09L TEXT:"disputa acirrada"] para o segundo turno de 25 de outubro, com Flávio, filho do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, mantendo uma ligeira vantagem após terminar quase 2 pontos percentuais à frente de Lula no [USN:L6N45N1A0 TEXT:"primeiro turno da eleição"], em 4 de outubro. Ambos os candidatos esperam conquistar os 33 milhões de eleitores que ficaram em casa no primeiro turno, o que equivale a cerca de um em cada cinco eleitores qualificados. O debate em São Paulo está marcado para começar às 20h e será transmitido pela emissora Band. O último debate do primeiro turno foi [USN:L1N45M12Z TEXT:"cancelado de última hora"], depois que Lula e Flávio desistiram de participar. Antes um marco da democracia brasileira após o fim da ditadura militar de 21 anos no país, em 1985, os debates presidenciais televisionados perderam relevância à medida que os principais candidatos passaram a optar cada vez mais por não participar. POLÍTICA ACIRRADA Espera-se que o debate entre Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula seja tenso e marcado por ataques pessoais. A polarização entre os apoiadores de Jair Bolsonaro e de Lula domina a política brasileira há quase uma década. Muitos bolsonaristas defendem que Lula deveria estar preso pelos escândalos de corrupção que envolveram o PT, enquanto muitos apoiadores de Lula argumentam que a condenação e a prisão do ex-presidente Bolsonaro por tentativa de golpe de Estado foram justificadas. "Eu não gosto de bandidos. Fora, Lula!", disse a manifestante Vera de Sousa, em São Paulo. No ato em São Paulo, participantes exibiam um grande boneco inflável de Lula vestido com roupa de presidiário. Já em Brasília, manifestantes entoavam gritos de "Bolsonaro na cadeia", enquanto uma imagem do ex-presidente o retratava com as mãos ensanguentadas. "Precisamos que o atual governo continue no poder. Se entrar outro governo, estamos, desculpe a expressão, ferrados", disse a apoiadora de Lula Sonia Maria, durante o ato em Brasília. Lula passou 580 dias preso entre 2018 e 2019 por uma condenação por corrupção que acabou sendo anulada devido a falhas nas investigações e nos procedimentos judiciais. Já o ex-presidente Bolsonaro foi condenado a 27 anos de prisão por conspirar para um golpe de Estado após perder a disputa pela reeleição para Lula em 2022. Ele cumpre a pena em prisão domiciliar por questões de saúde. O filho de Bolsonaro afirmou que o julgamento do pai foi uma "farsa" e prometeu buscar anistia para ele caso seja eleito presidente. "Faltam sete dias para livrarmos o Brasil do PT. E vocês verão Jair Messias Bolsonaro colocando a faixa de presidente no filho dele", disse Flávio à multidão em São Paulo. Em uma postagem na rede social X, Lula afirmou que quem votasse em seu oponente levaria, de "brinde", o pai e os irmãos dele. REVOLTA CONTRA META Uma polêmica sobre se as plataformas da Meta, que incluem o Facebook e o Instagram, trataram os dois candidatos de forma igualitária trouxe nova tensão aos últimos dias da campanha. A coalizão de Lula afirmou que sua conta no Instagram e suas publicações foram restringidas, e o jornal local Folha de S.Paulo divulgou mensagens internas de funcionários da Meta que admitiam [USN:S0N40000V TEXT:"essas restrições"] e afirmavam que a plataforma havia recomendado o perfil de Flávio e seu canal no WhatsApp aos usuários. A Meta afirmou ter enfrentado problemas técnicos globais, mas negou qualquer viés político. “Qualquer sugestão de que a Meta favoreça um lado é falsa”, disse a empresa. Organizações da sociedade civil planejavam realizar um protesto na segunda-feira em frente à sede da Meta em São Paulo contra a "interferência da empresa no processo eleitoral brasileiro", disseram os organizadores em comunicado. (Reportagem de Brendan O'Boyle e Luis Nova em Brasília, com reportagem adicional de Letícia Fucuchima e Sebastian Rocandio em São Paulo)

item.title: Milan police clash with protesters on second day of unrest
item.description: Milan police clashed on Sunday with protesters throwing stones and looting shops during demonstrations against poor services and the rising cost of living, a day after similar unrest in several Italian cities.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Milan police clashed on Sunday with protesters throwing stones and looting shops during demonstrations against poor services and the rising cost of living, a day after similar unrest in several Italian cities. Police in riot gear fired tear gas and used water cannons after several hundred hooded protesters broke shop windows and set bins on fire in the area near central Piazza Duomo, sources with knowledge of the investigation told Reuters. More than 60 protesters were taken to the police station for further checks, the sources added. A total of 28 protesters were arrested after similar clashes erupted on Saturday in northern cities including Milan, Bologna, Brescia, Bergamo and Turin, according to a police report on Sunday. The clashes had echoes of the [USN:L1N46401W TEXT:"violence in neighbouring France"], where hundreds of thousands of people angered by rising costs and declining public services took to the streets on Saturday in some of the country's most violent protests in years. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, facing an election next year, condemned the violence and announced a government meeting on Monday to discuss how to address the situation.

item.title: Barcelona Women suffer first defeat in 350 days
item.description: Barcelona's women suffered their first defeat in 350 days as Real Sociedad came from behind to claim a 2-1 Liga F victory at Zubieta on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Barcelona's women suffered their first defeat in 350 days as Real Sociedad came from behind to claim a 2-1 Liga F victory at Zubieta on Sunday. Patri Guijarro put Barcelona ahead inside the opening minute, but Cecilia Marcos equalised before Ainhoa Marin completed a memorable comeback for the Basque side. The defeat ended Barcelona's 45-game unbeaten run and was their first since a 1-0 loss to the same opponents last November. Barcelona lost only once last season as they swept the Champions League, Liga F, Copa de la Reina and Spanish Super Cup, while Sunday's setback was their first of the current campaign. They remain top of Liga F with 18 points, two ahead of second-placed Real Madrid, who beat Espanyol 3-1 on Saturday. Real Sociedad climbed to 11th on eight points after recording only their second victory of the season.

item.title: Papa Leão promete retorno gradual às funções no primeiro compromisso desde a cirurgia de câncer
item.description: O Papa Leão prometeu neste domingo retomar gradualmente suas atividades habituais como líder do 1,4 bilhão de católicos do mundo, ao saudar a multidão na Praça de São Pedro durante seu primeiro evento público desde que passou por uma cirurgia para tratar um câncer de pulmão, há cinco dias.
item.dc:creator: Joshua McElwee
item.content:encoded: O Papa Leão prometeu neste domingo retomar gradualmente suas atividades habituais como líder do 1,4 bilhão de católicos do mundo, ao saudar a multidão na Praça de São Pedro durante seu primeiro evento público desde que passou por uma cirurgia para tratar um câncer de pulmão, há cinco dias. O pontífice, de 71 anos, foi submetido a uma [USN:S8N42Y05U TEXT:"cirurgia"] na terça-feira para remover o lobo inferior do pulmão direito, [USN:L8N4600P9 TEXT:"o que alimentou especulações"] sobre como sua doença poderia alterar seus 17 meses de papado. Sorrindo de uma janela do Palácio Apostólico do Vaticano enquanto falava aos peregrinos abaixo com voz firme e clara neste domingo, o primeiro papa norte-americano agradeceu às pessoas de todo o mundo por suas orações e disse que agora começaria a retomar sua rotina normal. “Tendo superado essa fase delicada... agora retomarei gradualmente minhas atividades, sempre com a ajuda de Deus e de suas orações”, disse Leão. O papa, que recebeu alta do hospital Gemelli, em Roma, no sábado, chegou à janela do palácio sem ajuda e cumpriu seu compromisso semanal do meio-dia como de costume. Ele também exortou os peregrinos que aguardavam lá embaixo, sob um céu nublado, a deixarem de lado quaisquer ambições egoístas e a servirem a Deus “sem concessões”. FREIRA CHORA AO VER LEO APARECER Leão foi diagnosticado com [USN:L8N46006S TEXT:"adenocarcinoma de pulmão"], a forma mais comum de câncer de pulmão. O diagnóstico, para o papa mais jovem em décadas, eleito apenas em maio de 2025, causou comoção. Seus médicos deram alta a ele no sábado, depois que exames de sangue e imagens torácicas realizados naquele dia mostraram que ele estava bem o suficiente para voltar para casa. Os médicos afirmaram que ele era capaz de realizar atividades diárias normais de forma independente. A multidão na Praça de São Pedro, que somava cerca de 15 mil pessoas segundo o Vaticano, gritou e aplaudiu ruidosamente quando Leo apareceu pela primeira vez na janela no domingo. Uma freira católica se ajoelhou e chorou, cobrindo o rosto com as mãos. A poucos passos dali, um grupo de outras freiras erguia um cartaz com os dizeres: “Nossos melhores votos, Santo Padre. Nós o amamos e estamos rezando por você”. AGENDA DO PAPA EM MUDANÇA Leão costuma ter uma agenda lotada, mas o Vaticano cancelou seus outros eventos públicos até pelo menos quarta-feira, quando ele deve realizar uma audiência geral semanal na Praça de São Pedro. Não foi informado se ele realizará essa audiência. O papa também planeja visitar o Uruguai, a Argentina e o Peru de 6 a 17 de novembro, em uma das viagens mais intensas organizadas para um líder católico [USN:L8N45D0VL TEXT:"nas últimas décadas"]. O Dr. Stefano Margaritora, cirurgião-chefe do papa, disse no sábado que Leo poderia estar totalmente recuperado a tempo para essa viagem. O cardeal Pietro Parolin, secretário de Estado do Vaticano, expressou, no entanto, ceticismo. Ele disse a jornalistas na sexta-feira que o papa talvez precise ajustar o ritmo de sua agenda daqui para frente “de acordo com o estado de saúde”. (Reportagem de Joshua McElwee; Reportagem adicional de Matteo Minnella)

item.title: Ka'imi Fairbairn kicks Texans past Jaguars in London
item.description: CJ Stroud threw for 312 yards and three touchdowns to set the stage for Ka'imi Fairbairn's game-winning 49-yard field goal as time expired, helping the Houston Texans pull out a 34-31 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars Sunday in London.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: CJ Stroud threw for 312 yards and three touchdowns to set the stage for Ka'imi Fairbairn's game-winning 49-yard field goal as time expired, helping the Houston Texans pull out a 34-31 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars Sunday in London. Stroud completed 24 of 34 passes with one interception. Tight end Foster Moreau caught two passes, both touchdowns, while Jaylin Noel had a career-high 107 receiving yards and a touchdown for the Texans (2-4). Trevor Lawrence completed 24 of 41 passes for 306 yards, four touchdowns and one pick for the Jaguars (4-2), who had their three-game winning streak snapped. Bhayshul Tuten had 39 rushing yards and four catches for 48 yards and two TD catches. With Houston leading 31-28 late in the fourth quarter and driving toward a clinching score, Travis Hunter Jr. came away with an interception in the end zone. After he caught a touchdown pass on the prior possession, Hunter is the first NFL player since Brian Dawkins in 2002 with a TD catch and interception in the same game. That turnover set Cam Little up for a game-tying 60-yard field goal with 1:55 left. But Stroud found Woody Marks for a 19-yard gain to cross midfield, setting up Fairbairn's game-winner. Houston opened the scoring when Stroud connected with Moreau for a 6-yard score with 5:13 left in the first quarter. After a few squandered opportunities, the Jaguars leveled the score at 7-7 with 6:47 left in the first half on Lawrence's 27-yard connection with Tuten. The Texans responded with a 25-yard field goal from Fairbairn with 4:16 left in the first half, setting up a frantic finish to the first half. Lawrence found Tuten again, this time from 2 yards out, to give Jacksonville a 14-10 lead with 55 seconds left. However, a 50-yard pass from Stroud to Noel to begin the ensuing Houston drive set up a 1-yard TD catch by Moreau with eight seconds left to hand the Texans a 17-14 halftime edge. The back-and-forth blows continued in the second half, albeit with Houston keeping Jacksonville at arm's length. A 13-yard TD catch by Noel on the opening drive out of halftime gave the Texans a 24-14 lead. Lawrence found rookie tight end Nate Boerkircher for his first career TD to cut it to 24-21 with 2:34 left in the third. The Texans restored their two-score lead with Jawhar Jordan's 25-yard TD run. Jacksonville again responded with Lawrence finding Hunter for a 7-yard score to cut it to 31-28. --Field Level Media

item.title: Big 12 admits clock error in Notre Dame's loss to BYU
item.description: The Big 12 acknowledged that one second should have been placed back on the clock after what turned out to be the final play of the Notre Dame-BYU game on Saturday in Provo, Utah.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Big 12 acknowledged that one second should have been placed back on the clock after what turned out to be the final play of the Notre Dame-BYU game on Saturday in Provo, Utah. With four seconds remaining on the clock, Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr tossed an incomplete pass to Jaden Greathouse in the right corner of the end zone. Replays showed the ball hit the ground with one second remaining, but the clock still ran out in No. 8 BYU's 28-24 victory over No. 2 Notre Dame. "Following the Big 12's review of the final play of Saturday's Notre Dame-BYU game, it was determined that time remained on the clock when the ball hit the ground," the Big 12's statement read, "and the play was incorrectly cleared by the replay officiating crew. "The Conference will conduct a complete review of its end-of-game officiating process in advance of next week's games." As an FBS independent, Notre Dame has its games officiated by the conference of its opponent. --Field Level Media

item.title: Trump endorses Netanyahu in Israeli election
item.description: The Trump endorsement is not certain to give Netanyahu and his right-wing Likud party a boost as Israeli public support for Trump has diminished amid Israeli-US disagreements over Iran.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Trump endorses Netanyahu in Israeli election

The Trump endorsement is not certain to give Netanyahu and his right-wing Likud party a boost as Israeli public support for Trump has diminished amid Israeli-US disagreements over Iran.

US President Donald Trump points his finger towards Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as they shake hands during a press conference after meeting at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida, Dec 29, 2025. (Photo: REUTERS/Jonathan Ernst)

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Sunday (Oct 18) endorsed his ally Benjamin Netanyahu as the longtime Israeli prime minister struggles for an edge in next week's parliamentary election. Trump praised Netanyahu as a "great warrior prime minster" and peace partner, crediting him with joining the United States in launching strikes on Iran in February. The conflict, in its seventh month, has disrupted energy markets globally and wreaked havoc across the Middle East, damaging critical infrastructure and destabilising regional economies. "Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself," Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social. "Despite all of that, he has endured and, in fact, he has thrived! I have watched Bibi under the most trying of times. Normal men or women in such situations would have wilted under the pressure - But Bibi did not wilt, he actually got stronger, and maintains that same Strength today."

In his message, addressed to "the Great People of Israel," Trump added, "Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu in his upcoming Race for Re-Election as Prime Minister of Israel." The Trump endorsement is not certain to give Netanyahu and his right-wing Likud party a boost in the Oct 27 national election, as Israeli public support for Trump has diminished amid Israeli-US disagreements over Iran.

Related:

Trump rules out new Iran attack before US midterm elections

Israel top court puts Arab parties back on ballot

Polls have suggested no candidate has a clear path to power. Israel's prime minister is chosen through coalition-building in parliament rather than by direct popular vote. It will be Israel's first vote since the Hamas attack on Oct 7, 2023, that shook the country and plunged the Middle East into turmoil, as Israel went to war in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. The election could determine whether Netanyahu remains in power after one of the most consequential periods in Israel’s history, or is defeated by centrist rivals promising to usher in a new era. Netanyahu promptly expressed his thanks to Trump on X, saying, "Together we will complete the mission!" Trump has broken with longtime US tradition by endorsing candidates in elections in foreign countries, including Hungary, Colombia, Argentina, Japan and Honduras.

Source: Reuters/fs
