item.title: Brazil's Bolsonaro, Lula face off in first debate as supporters fill streets
item.description: Brazilians demonstrated for and against their presidential candidates on Sunday as President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro prepared to meet in their first televised debate with just one week left in the campaign.
item.dc:creator: Brendan O'Boyle, Sebastian Recondio, Luis Nova
item.content:encoded: Brazilians demonstrated for and against their presidential candidates on Sunday as President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro prepared to meet in their first televised debate with just one week left in the campaign. Pro-Bolsonaro crowds wearing Brazil's national colors of yellow, green and blue packed Paulista Avenue in Sao Paulo's financial center, where the candidate addressed the crowd. Lula supporters wearing red, symbolic of his Workers' Party, filled Brasilia's plaza of government buildings, and students backing the president protested against Bolsonaro in Rio de Janeiro. Polls show a [USN:S0N45N09L TEXT:"close race"] for the October 25 runoff, with Bolsonaro, son of former far-right President Jair Bolsonaro, holding a slight advantage after finishing nearly 2 percentage points ahead of leftist Lula in the [USN:L6N45N1A0 TEXT:"election's first round"] on October 4. Both candidates hope to engage the 33 million voters who stayed home in the election's first round, equal to about one in five eligible voters. The debate in Sao Paulo is scheduled to begin at 8 p.m. (2300 GMT) and air on broadcaster Band. The last debate in the election's first round was [USN:L1N45M12Z TEXT:"canceled at the last minute"] when Lula and Bolsonaro pulled out. Once a hallmark of Brazilian democracy following the end of the country's 21-year military dictatorship in 1985, televised presidential debates have lost relevance as leading candidates have increasingly chosen to stay away. BITTER POLITICS The debate between Senator Bolsonaro and President Lula is expected to be tense and personal. Bitter polarization between supporters of the elder Bolsonaro and Lula has dominated Brazilian politics for nearly a decade. Many Bolsonaro supporters believe Lula should be jailed over corruption scandals that ensnared his Workers' Party, while many Lula backers argue former President Bolsonaro's conviction and imprisonment for a coup attempt were warranted. "I don't like bandits. Out with Lula!" said demonstrator Vera de Sousa in Sao Paulo. At the Sao Paulo rally, crowd members held aloft a large inflatable of Lula in a prisoner's uniform, while rallygoers in Brasilia chanted "Bolsonaro in jail" and an effigy of Bolsonaro showed the former president with bloody hands. "We need the current government to remain in power. If another government comes in, we're, excuse my language, screwed," said Lula supporter Sonia Maria at the Brasilia rally. Lula spent 580 days in prison in 2018-2019 for a corruption conviction that was later overturned because of flaws in the investigations and legal proceedings. Former President Bolsonaro, meanwhile, received a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after losing his reelection bid to Lula in 2022. He is serving that underhouse arrest due to health issues. The younger Bolsonaro has said his father's trial was a "farce" and has promised to seek amnesty for him if elected president. "There are seven days left until we free Brazil from (Lula's) Workers’ Party. And you will see Jair Messias Bolsonaro placing the presidential sash on his son," Bolsonaro told the crowd in Sao Paulo. In a post on X, Lula said that anyone who voted for his opponent would get his father and brothers as a "bonus gift." ANGER OVER META A dispute over whether Meta’s platforms, which include Facebook and Instagram, treated the two candidates equally has injected new tension into the campaign's final days. Lula’s coalition said his Instagram account and posts were restricted, and local newspaper Folha de S.Paulo reported internal Meta messages that acknowledged [USN:S0N40000V TEXT:"those restrictions"] and said the platform had recommended Bolsonaro’s profile and WhatsApp channel to users. Meta said it had experienced global technical glitches but denied any political bias. “Any suggestion that Meta favors one side is false,” the company said. Civil society groups were planning a protest for Monday at Meta's main office in Sao Paulo, against "the company’s interference in the Brazilian electoral process," its organizers said in a press release.

item.title: Trump respalda a Netanyahu en las elecciones de Israel
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, respaldó este domingo a su aliado Benjamin Netanyahu, mientras el veterano primer ministro israelí lucha por hacerse con ventaja de cara a las elecciones parlamentarias de la próxima semana.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, respaldó este domingo a su aliado Benjamin Netanyahu, mientras el veterano primer ministro israelí lucha por hacerse con ventaja de cara a las elecciones parlamentarias de la próxima semana. Trump elogió a Netanyahu como un "gran primer ministro guerrero" y socio por la paz, y le reconoció el mérito de haberse unido a EEUU en los ataques contra Irán llevados a cabo en febrero. El conflicto, que ya cumple siete meses, ha trastornado los mercados energéticos a nivel mundial y ha causado estragos en todo Oriente Medio, dañando infraestructuras críticas y desestabilizando las economías regionales. "Bibi Netanyahu se ha mostrado fuerte, valiente y brillante frente a una tremenda oposición, incluida la procedente incluso del propio Israel", escribió Trump en una publicación en Truth Social. "A pesar de todo ello, ha resistido y, de hecho, ¡ha salido airoso! He observado a Bibi en los momentos más difíciles. Cualquier hombre o mujer normal en tales situaciones se habría derrumbado bajo la presión, pero Bibi no se derrumbó; de hecho, se hizo más fuerte y mantiene esa misma fortaleza hoy en día". En su mensaje, dirigido al "gran pueblo de Israel", Trump añadió: "Que esta carta sirva para expresar mi apoyo total y absoluto a Bibi Netanyahu en su próxima campaña para la reelección como primer ministro de Israel". No es seguro que el respaldo de Trump suponga un impulso para Netanyahu y su partido de derecha, el Likud, en las elecciones nacionales del 27 de octubre, ya que el apoyo público israelí a Trump ha disminuido en medio de los desacuerdos entre Israel y EEUU sobre Irán. Las encuestas sugieren que ningún candidato tiene un camino claro hacia el poder. El primer ministro de Israel se elige mediante la formación de una coalición en el Parlamento, y no por voto popular directo. Serán las primeras elecciones en Israel desde el ataque de Hamás del 7 de octubre de 2023, que sacudió al país y sumió a Oriente Medio en el caos, al entrar Israel en guerra en Gaza, el Líbano e Irán. Las elecciones podrían determinar si Netanyahu permanece en el poder tras uno de los períodos más trascendentales de la historia de Israel, o si es derrotado por rivales centristas que prometen marcar el comienzo de una nueva era. Netanyahu no tardó en expresar su agradecimiento a Trump en X, afirmando: "¡Juntos completaremos la misión!". Trump ha roto con una larga tradición estadounidense al respaldar a candidatos en elecciones de países extranjeros, entre ellos Hungría, Colombia, Argentina, Japón y Honduras. El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, expresó el domingo su apoyo a su aliado Benjamin Netanyahu de cara a las próximas elecciones parlamentarias israelíes.

item.title: Captain of flydubai plane describes blocking axe blows as co-pilot attacked
item.description: The captain of a flydubai flight who was attacked by a co-pilot who intended to crash the plane has described blocking axe blows to the head and screaming for help as he reached for a knob to open the cockpit door.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The captain of a flydubai flight who was attacked by a co-pilot who intended to crash the plane has described blocking axe blows to the head and screaming for help as he reached for a knob to open the cockpit door. Captain Smit Machchhar has been hailed as a hero for his role in averting disaster on the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv last month, helping to thwart what the UAE attorney general has said was an [USN:L6N45V0UP TEXT:"attempted suicide attack"] by the co-pilot who intended to crash the plane into Ben Gurion Airport. Speaking in an interview with The National newspaper from a hospital bed in Abu Dhabi, his head and left arm bandaged, Machchhar said that when the first blow landed, he thought something had gone "horribly wrong the aircraft structure", before quickly realising he was being attacked and things had "taken a drastic turn". "The next thought was I need to get help in here," he said in the interview published on Saturday. "My immediate action was to free myself from the seat belts and I tried to just block the blows as much as I could," he said, pointing to his arm that was wounded as he defended himself. "The blows were coming on the head." "Immediately my hand went to the knob which opens the door and screaming for my colleagues, screaming his name." "I believe that was the first time when I lost my consciousness." The aircraft, flight FZ1073, was in Saudi airspace when the co-pilot attacked Machchhar with a crash axe, typically kept in the cockpit for emergency use. The incident caused the airliner to plunge 16,000 feet (4,900 meters) in 30 seconds before the attacker was overwhelmed and two other pilots who were on board landed the aircraft safely in Saudi Arabia. The suspect, an Omani national, was transferred to the UAE, flydubai's home country. The plan was inspired by the September 11, 2001, attacks on the US, UAE public prosecutors say, as a result of their criminal investigation launched on October 1. Machchhar said he heard the cockpit door opening and screaming "between my colleague and the guy". He said the scariest thing he felt was the aircraft nose "steeply going down." "I was not very sure that I'll make it out alive from this. Did I give up? No."

item.title: Tensões voltam a crescer em Paris enquanto França contabiliza os custos da pior onda de distúrbios em anos
item.description: Novos confrontos eclodiram em Paris neste domingo, um dia depois de a França ter vivido um dos piores dias de agitação dos últimos anos, com protestos contra os preços altos que deixaram um manifestante morto, milhares de pessoas presas e lojas saqueadas ou danificadas em todo o país.
item.dc:creator: Sybille de La Hamaide
item.content:encoded: Novos confrontos eclodiram em Paris neste domingo, um dia depois de a França ter vivido um dos piores dias de agitação dos últimos anos, com protestos contra os preços altos que deixaram um manifestante morto, milhares de pessoas presas e lojas saqueadas ou danificadas em todo o país. Manifestações em todo o país se transformaram em tumultos no sábado, com uma prefeitura incendiada, lojas saqueadas e prédios cobertos de pichações, enquanto grupos violentos entraram em confronto com a polícia em cidades por todo o país. Um manifestante morreu após sofrer uma parada cardíaca durante [USN:L1N46302B TEXT:"os protestos"] em Paris. A polícia realizou mais de 2.000 prisões em toda a França, enquanto mais de 600 policiais ficaram feridos, informou o ministro do Interior. “Aqui parece uma zona de guerra”, disse o empresário holandês Tije De Boer, que havia vindo a Paris com seus filhos para visitar um amigo e afirmou que os protestos o forçaram a evacuar seu hotel na Place de la République, um dos pontos mais conturbados no sábado. A polícia voltou a lançar gás lacrimogêneo contra os manifestantes na Place de la République e bicicletas foram incendiadas na tarde de domingo, um sinal de que as tensões ainda não haviam se acalmado totalmente na capital. Mais de meio milhão de pessoas participaram de marchas em dezenas de cidades no sábado, marcando a convergência de um [USN:L6N45M1EJ TEXT:"movimento estudantil"] que já dura um mês com um descontentamento social mais amplo contra o aumento do custo de vida e o declínio dos serviços públicos. O presidente Emmanuel Macron fará um pronunciamento à nação às 20h, horário local, no domingo, informou seu gabinete. Os distúrbios de sábado revelaram a profunda raiva contra Macron, que deixará o cargo em 2027 após uma década no poder cada vez mais marcada pelo descontentamento social, uma economia fraca e uma dívida galopante. O governo atribuiu a violência a grupos de extrema esquerda e ultra-esquerda, bem como a criminosos que, segundo o governo, instigaram os saques. O líder da extrema direita francesa, Jordan Bardella, afirmou que a França havia sido “humilhada” e pediu que Macron renunciasse. “Estamos pagando por décadas de negligência, perda de autoridade e pelo desarmamento moral, psicológico e material de nossas forças de segurança interna”, disse ele durante visita a uma delegacia de polícia em Paris. VÁRIAS CENTENAS DE LOJAS DANIFICADAS Enquanto centenas de milhares protestavam pacificamente, grupos marginais violentos atacaram prédios públicos, saquearam butiques de luxo e supermercados e atacaram veículos e policiais. Uma operação maciça de limpeza teve início em cidades que vão de Lille, no norte, a Marselha, no sul, e de Estrasburgo, no leste, a Bordeaux, no sudoeste, onde uma multidão mascarada invadiu a residência do prefeito local. O ministro do Interior, Laurent Nunez, afirmou que várias centenas de lojas foram danificadas no sábado. Em [USN:L1N46402C TEXT:"Limoges"], no sudoeste da França, o prefeito Guillaume Guerin denunciou o caos após a prefeitura da cidade, de 143 anos, ter sido incendiada e amplamente destruída em um ataque criminoso no sábado, o que gerou comparações com o incêndio de 2019 que devastou a Catedral de Notre-Dame, em Paris. “Houve uma intenção clara e premeditada de incendiar a prefeitura, e as pessoas que estavam lá dentro temeram por suas vidas”, disse Guerin à Reuters. Ele ameaçou renunciar caso a cidade não recebesse os recursos necessários para reparar a prefeitura. ELEIÇÃO PRESIDENCIAL ACONTECERÁ NO PRÓXIMO ANO Os distúrbios aumentaram a pressão sobre o presidente Macron e seu governo antes da eleição presidencial prevista para o próximo ano. O primeiro-ministro Sébastien Lecornu atribuiu os distúrbios à “extrema esquerda” e aos criminosos. O ministro da Economia, Roland Lescure, prometeu apoio no domingo aos empresários que sofreram prejuízos. “Quem destruir coisas vai pagar, reparar os danos e ser responsabilizado por sua intenção de semear o caos”, disse Lescure em comunicado. O prefeito de Bordeaux, Thomas Cazenave, disse que até 100 lojas foram saqueadas em sua cidade, enquanto o prefeito de Marselha, Benoit Payan, anunciou ajuda financeira de emergência para apoiar as empresas afetadas pela violência. O presidente-executivo da rede francesa de varejo Carrefour (CARR.PA) , Alexandre Bompard, disse à emissora francesa BFMTV que 50 lojas da empresa foram danificadas, incluindo 20 que foram saqueadas, com prejuízos decorrentes dos danos chegando a dezenas de milhões de euros. Os protestos começaram no mês passado devido às condições das escolas e à escassez de professores nos subúrbios da classe trabalhadora, antes de se transformarem em um movimento contra a desigualdade, os cortes nos gastos públicos e o aumento do custo de vida. (Reportagem de Sybille de La Hamaide; Reportagem adicional de Natasa Bansagi, Janis Laizans, Abdul Saboor e Clotaire Achi)

item.title: Trump apporte son soutien à Netanyahu pour les élections en Israël
item.description: Le président américain Donald Trump a apporté dimanche son soutien à Benjamin Netanyahu en vue des prochaines élections législatives israéliennes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le président américain Donald Trump a apporté dimanche son soutien à Benjamin Netanyahu en vue des prochaines élections législatives israéliennes. "Bibi Netanyahu s’est montré fort, courageux et brillant face à une opposition farouche, y compris celle venant d’Israël même", a écrit Donald Trump dans un message publié sur son réseau Truth Social. "C’est le genre de partenaire que les États-Unis d’Amérique attendent d’Israël, un pays pour lequel ils ont tant fait. Que cette lettre témoigne de mon soutien total et inconditionnel à Bibi Netanyahu dans sa prochaine campagne pour sa réélection au poste de Premier ministre d’Israël." Les élections législatives se dérouleront le 27 octobre. Il s'agira du premier scrutin depuis les attaques du Hamas le 7 octobre 2023 et la coalition au pouvoir apparaît en difficulté dans les sondages d'intention de vote.

item.title: Barcelona hit by double injury blow before PSG trip
item.description: Barcelona coach Hansi Flick was dealt a double blow ahead of a crucial week after the club confirmed injuries to defenders Jules Kounde and Eric Garcia on social media on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Barcelona coach Hansi Flick was dealt a double blow ahead of a crucial week after the club confirmed injuries to defenders Jules Kounde and Eric Garcia on social media on Sunday. The Catalan side visit Paris St Germain in the Champions League on Tuesday and host Real Madrid in El Clasico next Sunday. Garcia was ruled out for three to four weeks with a thigh injury Kounde will also miss the PSG game with an ankle sprain, but could return against Real Madrid Gerard Martin exited Saturday's 5-2 win over Real Betis at halftime, but was not included in the club's Sunday medical update Andreas Christensen is already out injured, leaving only Martin and Pau Cubarsi as natural options at centre back for the PSG game

item.title: Four dead, 39 injured at Canadian military base in grass fire fanned by high winds, officials say
item.description: A fire that killed at least four soldiers and left 19 people in critical condition began with a smoldering grass fire that ignited in an Alberta military base's training area where personnel were drilling, Canadian officials said Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Amanda Stephenson
item.content:encoded: A fire that killed at least four soldiers and left 19 people in critical condition began with a smoldering grass fire that ignited in an Alberta military base's training area where personnel were drilling, Canadian officials said Sunday. Officials said 39 people were in hospitals as a result of the fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, which began around 4 p.m. MDT (2200 GMT) on Saturday. Winds up to 60 miles per hour (96 kilometers per hour) fed the flames. Major General Wade Rutland described the fire as an "uncommon, rapid" event. “I’ve certainly never seen anything like it," said Rutland, commander of 1st Canadian Division, which is based in Edmonton, about 210 km (130 miles) west of the military site. Prime Minister Mark Carney said earlier Sunday that the fire was one of the worst peacetime tragedies ever for Canada's armed forces on home soil. "The nation is in mourning for those brave members of our Armed Forces whom we have lost," Carney said Sunday, adding that he had ordered flags on federal buildings across the country to be lowered to half-staff to honor the victims. CFB Wainwright had 1,310 military and civilian personnel stationed there as of 2021, according to census data. National Defence Minister David McGuinty said on Sunday he would go to the city for briefings on the situation. The base houses the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre, which runs training scenarios and exercises for the army. Carney said those affected in Saturday's fire came from military bases across the country. Military and civilian firefighters fought the fire through the night in "some of the worst conditions imaginable," Carney said. Air ambulances from Edmonton and Saskatoon, which is about 300 km from Wainwright, flew to the military base on Saturday, Carney said. Patients are being treated in Edmonton, Wainwright, Calgary and Red Deer, he said. Health staff in Edmonton said a "code orange," or mass-casualty event, was declared to coordinate the medical response for patients being transported from Wainwright, CBC News reported. The town of Wainwright, with a population of about 6,600, is just north of the base. The municipality posted on social media that the fire had crossed the base fence into the nearby district but no evacuation orders had been issued. It said on Sunday that the fire is not expected to spread beyond its current boundaries.

item.title: Man United show fight but familiar flaws remain in Leeds draw
item.description: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick took heart from his team's resilience in Sunday's 1-1 Premier League draw at Leeds United, but his description of the result as a "step forward" underlined how far expectations have fallen during a difficult spell for the club.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick took heart from his team's resilience in Sunday's 1-1 Premier League draw at Leeds United, but his description of the result as a "step forward" underlined how far expectations have fallen during a difficult spell for the club. One win from seven league games has left United languishing in 13th, a stark contrast to last season's third-place finish and evidence that their problems run deeper than a difficult week. Carrick conceded they had fallen short of the quality they are capable of producing, particularly on the ball, but he found encouragement in the discipline and togetherness his players showed in the pressure of a fierce rivalry at Elland Road. "Maybe if you talk about top quality, maybe it wasn't top, top quality I think we are capable of playing," Carrick said. "With the results we've had we weren't quite flowing but there's enough in there to take from it." The greater significance for Carrick appeared to lie in how United responded to adversity. After being outplayed in a 1-1 draw with bottom side Tottenham Hotspur last weekend and losing 2-0 at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League, the build-up to Sunday's game was further complicated by [USN:L8N4612C3 TEXT:"Lisandro Martinez"] publicly criticising the club hierarchy before apologising. Against that backdrop, Carrick placed greater emphasis on structure than style. United were harder to break down, and he praised his players for sticking to their roles and responsibilities in what he described as a tense game that could have gone either way. "It's a bit more than just effort," Carrick said. "It is the way you go about it. The plan. The responsibilities. The roles. I thought the boys took that responsibility on really well for the most part." FAMILIAR SHORTCOMINGS Yet familiar shortcomings remained. United surrendered their lead from a set piece and lacked enough quality in possession to take control of the match, leaving Carrick with another draw rather than the victory his side badly needed. After a week dominated as much by events off the pitch as those on it, however, Carrick was keen to stress that the dressing room remained united. "I suppose you're looking at the togetherness, the spirit, the unit. I don't doubt that within the group," he said. "The way that we went about it today gives me a lot of belief in us moving forward." United head to Como for a Champions League game on Wednesday.

item.title: Woman dies after being swept away by river as torrential rains batter Spain
item.description: A woman died after she was swept away trying to cross a river in torrential rain in Spain's northeastern Catalonia region, authorities said on Sunday, bringing to five the death toll from heavy rain and flooding over the past 15 days.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A woman died after she was swept away trying to cross a river in torrential rain in Spain's northeastern Catalonia region, authorities said on Sunday, bringing to five the death toll from heavy rain and flooding over the past 15 days. The 35-year-old was swept away in Cabrera de Mar, about 27 km (17 miles) north of Barcelona, as she tried to cross a river with her children on Saturday night, despite warnings not to go near waterways. Óscar Fernández, the Cabrera de Mar mayor, told reporters on Sunday that the woman had been to see a basketball match at which people were asked not to leave the municipal facility because of the torrential rain. Roads were closed and train services reduced, as Catalan authorities warned residents not to travel unnecessarily. The woman's body was found on Sunday by rescuers in the sea, the Civil Protection Service said. Flooding is becoming more frequent across Europe as the atmosphere warms and holds more moisture due to climate change, scientists say. Spain has been particularly hard hit. Valencia and Alicante in the country's southeast and Almeria in the south have also been affected by torrential rains which flooded homes, washed away cars and closed roads. "It started raining, it was fast. This stream carried a lot of water and it filled up really fast. The problem was that there were cars in the middle of the highway. It washed them away,” Beatriz Mendoza, who owns a commercial greenhouse in Almeria which was destroyed by the rain, told Canalsur, a local television station on Sunday. In August, a flood and landslide caused by torrential rain [USN:L8N44D01F TEXT:"killed two elderly women"] near Pontevedra in rural northwestern Spain, as seven regions were placed on yellow alert for storms and heavy rain. The flooding followed weeks of record high temperatures that led to a series of devastating wildfires.

item.title: Leverkusen's Schick strikes to end Freiburg's unbeaten run
item.description: Bayer Leverkusen netted a 76th-minute winner through leading scorer Patrik Schick to beat Freiburg 2-1 on Sunday and move into the top four of the Bundesliga standings.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bayer Leverkusen netted a 76th-minute winner through leading scorer Patrik Schick to beat Freiburg 2-1 on Sunday and move into the top four of the Bundesliga standings. Czech striker Schick, who became the first Leverkusen player to score in each of the first six matches of a season, tapped in after superb work from Ibrahim Maza, as his team moved to 13 points, behind Freiburg on goal difference. Bayern Munich, on 14, took over at the top following their 6-1 [USN:L6N46305Y TEXT:"demolition"] of RB Leipzig on Saturday. Dortmund are in second place, also on 14. Freiburg, who suffered their first loss of the season across all competitions and face Bayern next week, took a 14th-minute lead through Derry Scherhant, with Germany coach Juergen Klopp watching from the stands. It only lasted five minutes, however, with Ibrahim Maza bagging the equaliser. Neither team had big chances after the break until Maza shook off three markers near the corner line with dazzling skills to cut back for Schick to tap home.

item.title: US officials visit Palestinian village after settler attacks on diplomats
item.description: While Foreign Minister Gideon Saar and the Israeli military blamed "Israeli rioters" for the attack, Benjamin Netanyahu, whose coalition is projected to lose its governing majority, has been more circumspect.
item.dc:creator: Ali Sawafta, Steven Scheer
item.content:encoded: US diplomats visited a Christian Palestinian village in the Israeli-occupied West Bank on Sunday following attacks by militant Israeli settlers on [USN:L1N46305Z TEXT:"European diplomats"] and an [USN:L1N4620BI TEXT:"American photojournalist"] in the previous two days. Riley Barnes, assistant secretary of state for democracy, human rights and labor, Brian Burch, US ambassador to the Holy See, and a number of other diplomats visited the Latin Convent church and were expected to meet with members of the Christian community in Taybeh. Belgian, French and Polish diplomats, along with a French mayor and Palestinian civilians, had been attacked near Taybeh on Saturday by masked Israeli settlers. The previous day, Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine was taken to hospital after being assaulted while covering a Palestinian olive harvest near another West Bank village. The diplomats' visit coincided with US President Donald Trump [USN:L1N46403J TEXT:"endorsing"] his ally, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, for Israel's parliamentary election on October 27. Meanwhile, US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee attended a settler conference in the West Bank on Sunday. Huckabee, an evangelical Christian and longtime supporter of Israel, earlier wrote on X calling for "those who attacked" the Washington Post photojournalist, a US citizen, to be jailed. NETANYAHU CIRCUMSPECT ON SETTLER VIOLENCE Trump has expressed his opposition to Israeli annexation of the West Bank, but his administration has put little [USN:L6N45G09W TEXT:"pressure on Netanyahu's"] right-wing, pro-settler government to change its policy. UN bodies and most countries deem the settlements illegal under international law, but Israel rejects this, viewing the territory as disputed rather than occupied. While Foreign Minister Gideon Saar and the Israeli military both blamed "Israeli rioters" for the attack on the diplomats, Netanyahu, whose coalition is projected to lose its governing majority, has been more circumspect. He has said the diplomats entered a "sensitive area with a history of confrontations without prior coordination" with the Israeli military, and that the facts of the attack on Levine are "unclear". France urged Israeli authorities to arrest Saturday's attackers and to end criminal violence in the West Bank, but by Sunday there was no announcement from Israeli authorities of any arrests in either of the two latest incidents. The West Bank is home to some 500,000 settlers and at least 3 million Palestinians. Settler attacks on the Palestinians are surging, with at least 170 since September 27, according to Yesh Din, an Israeli human rights group. Journalists, activists and foreign observers have also been targeted. Yet prosecutions of Israeli settlers are rare. On Sunday, Reuters saw a group of at least 10 settlers, masked and dressed in black, hurling rocks at Palestinians and activists harvesting olives near the Palestinian West Bank town of Salfit, prompting the farmers to flee. Israeli border police were in the area and shot tear gas towards the hills.

item.title: Brighton's Gomez scores spectacular goal from halfway line
item.description: Diego Gomez produced a stunning halfway-line goal as Brighton & Hove Albion thrashed Crystal Palace 5-0 on Sunday, the Premier League's longest-range strike in nearly nine years.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Diego Gomez produced a stunning halfway-line goal as Brighton & Hove Albion thrashed Crystal Palace 5-0 on Sunday, the Premier League's longest-range strike in nearly nine years. With Brighton 1-0 up following an early own goal from Jaydee Canvot, Gomez spotted Palace goalkeeper Walter Benitez off his line in the seventh minute and seized his opportunity from the centre circle. The Paraguayan midfielder took one touch before unleashing a spectacular shot from 51 metres out, leaving the backtracking Benitez desperately flailing his arms as the ball sailed over him and into the back of the net. Gomez's audacious strike was the furthest range goal in the Premier League since Wayne Rooney scored for Everton against West Ham United from 58 metres out in November 2017, according to data firm Opta. "When I got the ball I knew the goalkeeper was a little bit ahead. When I scored, I didn't know where to run or what to do. I was very happy with the goal," Gomez told Sky Sports. "It's about the brotherhood and the intensity. We keep doing this in training and games." Former goalkeeper and BBC pundit Shay Given said he could not blame Benitez for the goal. "We're always talking about sweeper goalkeepers and you've got to be high up for the through ball and the defence playing a high line. I think his position was fine," Given said. "You've just got to take your hat off to Gomez. That is just a brilliant, brilliant goal." Brighton continued to run riot and moved to the top of the scoring charts with 23 goals in seven games this season. They are provisionally second in the standings, five points behind leaders Manchester City.

item.title: Man City beat Brighton, Chelsea hammer Spurs in WSL
item.description: Manchester City held off a spirited comeback from Brighton & Hove Albion on Sunday to secure a 3-2 win that maintained their perfect start to the Women's Super League season, with Chelsea close behind after a convincing win over Tottenham Hotspur.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Manchester City held off a spirited comeback from Brighton & Hove Albion on Sunday to secure a 3-2 win that maintained their perfect start to the Women's Super League season, with Chelsea close behind after a convincing win over Tottenham Hotspur. City raced into a 3-0 lead by the 17th minute thanks to a brace from Bunny Shaw and a goal from Niamh Charles, and though Brighton pulled two goals back before the break through Olivia Garcia and Caitlin Hayes, neither side managed to find the net again in the second half. City have 18 points from six games, two ahead of Chelsea after their 6-2 demolition of Tottenham. Lauren James and Ellie Carpenter both scored twice for the Blues against Spurs, who only let in two goals while collecting three wins and a draw in their first four games but have now conceded six in each of their last two league clashes. London City Lionesses remained third after a 2-1 win at home to Everton, while Manchester United's 3-1 win over bottom side Charlton Athletic left them in fifth place on 10 points, behind Tottenham on goal difference. Aston Villa put daylight between themselves and the drop zone by coming back from a goal down to beat Liverpool 2-1 and record their first victory of the season to move into 10th spot, above Crystal Palace, who lost 1-0 at home to West Ham United, on goal difference. Arsenal's stumbling start to the season continued on Saturday as they were held to a 1-1 draw by Birmingham City to leave them winless in their last five WSL games, fans at the Emirates greeting the final whistle with boos after the Gunners had to come from behind to salvage a point. Arsenal's streak of five league games without a win is their worst in the WSL era, and next up is a North London derby against Tottenham.

item.title: Arsenal edge Forest with late goal, Man United held by Leeds
item.description: Champions Arsenal needed a late goal from Noni Madueke, their only shot on target, to scrape a 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest on Sunday and remain three points behind Premier League leaders Manchester City.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Champions Arsenal needed a late goal from Noni Madueke, their only shot on target, to scrape a 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest on Sunday and remain three points behind Premier League leaders Manchester City. Brighton & Hove Albion's Diego Gomez struck a sensational goal from inside his own half in a 5-0 rout of Crystal Palace on Sunday to leave his side third in the table with 16 points, five behind leaders Manchester City. Manchester United and bitter rivals Leeds United shared the spoils in a 1-1 draw at Elland Road at the end of a turbulent week for the Red Devils in which defender Lisandro Martinez had publicly challenged the club's hierarchy. Leeds are seventh in the table and Manchester United, who have just one win from seven games, are 13th. Bournemouth beat Sunderland 2-0 for their first league victory of the season to climb to 15th place. Sunderland remained in the drop zone in 19th place. At the City Ground, a frustrated Arsenal finally sealed victory in the 80th minute. Ibrahim Sangare hesitated when he could have cleared the ball, leaving Forest manager Oliver Glasner visibly fuming, and second-half substitute Madueke then danced past Daniel Munoz before hammering a shot that deflected off Jair Cunha and wrong-footed Matz Sels. "We're really happy, we did it all together. We showed grit, determination, and maybe we showed a champion spirit here for that, really pleased," Madueke told Sky Sports. Murillo almost salvaged a point for Forest in injury time when he beat three players before unleashing a shot that sailed agonisingly wide. The defeat left Forest, who have yet to win or even score at the City Ground this season, in the drop zone in 18th place with five points. At the Amex, Brighton got on the scoresheet in the fourth minute through a Jaydee Canvot own goal, before Gomez struck a goal of the season contender three minutes later, robbing Adam Wharton of the ball near the halfway line before taking a touch and firing the ball over keeper Walter Benitez and into the net. "When I got the ball I knew the goalkeeper was a little bit ahead," Gomez told Sky Sports. "When I scored I didn't know where to run or what to do. I was very happy with the goal." Yasin Ayari padded Brighton's lead three minutes later, before Charalampos Kostoulas and Jack Hinshelwood completed the rout after the break. Kostoulas scored just after halftime when Ayari's shot deflected into the Greece international's path, and Hinshelwood struck in the 84th when Luka Vuskovic's header was scooped off the line by Benitez and he fired home the rebound. MBEUMO GRABS OPENING GOAL Manchester United looked on course for a much-needed victory when Bryan Mbeumo scored in the 35th minute after missing a couple of chances. Mbeumo held off James Justin before tapping in a Youri Tielemans cross from six yards out. Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised in the 51st minute, chesting down the ball from a corner before poking home. "We are slightly disappointed it is just a point," Leeds boss Daniel Farke told Sky. "Second half, we got the equaliser, we should have kept up the dominance, too many strikes went over the crossbar but it was overall a solid performance. "We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month if we were seen as favourites against Manchester United." Manchester defender Martinez retained his place in Michael Carrick's starting lineup despite criticising United's hierarchy following Tuesday's 2-0 Champions League defeat at Atletico Madrid, questioning the club’s summer investment and singling out director of football Jason Wilcox before later apologising. Bournemouth punished a shaky Sunderland start to take the lead after just six minutes, when Lewis Cook lofted a long ball forward that Evanilson ran on to and squared for Marcus Tavernier to head home from close range. Evanilson scored himself in the 48th minute when the Brazilian rounded goalkeeper Robin Roefs before slotting home left-footed.

item.title: PSG's Mendes sustains thigh injury ahead of Barcelona clash
item.description: Paris St Germain left back Nuno Mendes will be sidelined for weeks after suffering a thigh injury, the Ligue 1 champions said on Sunday, dealing a blow to their preparations for Tuesday's Champions League home game against Barcelona.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Paris St Germain left back Nuno Mendes will be sidelined for weeks after suffering a thigh injury, the Ligue 1 champions said on Sunday, dealing a blow to their preparations for Tuesday's Champions League home game against Barcelona. The 24-year-old Portugal international sustained the injury during [USN:L1N46307H TEXT:"PSG's 3-1 Ligue 1 victory"] at Strasbourg on Saturday. "Nuno Mendes, who suffered an injury to his left thigh during last night's match against RC Strasbourg Alsace, will be unavailable for the next few weeks," PSG said in a statement. Mendes has make seven appearances across all competitions this season. The back-to-back European champions sit top of the standings with maximum points from their opening two matches. Barcelona are second, also on six points.

item.title: Rubio afirma que Trump levará até 60 dias para avaliar as sanções contra a Rússia
item.description: Um dia após suspender sanções e tarifas relacionadas às exportações russas, o presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmou no sábado que ainda não tomou uma decisão final sobre o assunto, enquanto o secretário de Estado, Marco Rubio, disse que as autoridades querem mais tempo para avaliar a situação.
item.dc:creator: Nandita Bose, Gram Slattery
item.content:encoded: Um dia após suspender sanções e tarifas relacionadas às exportações russas, o presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmou no sábado que ainda não tomou uma decisão final sobre o assunto, enquanto o secretário de Estado, Marco Rubio, disse que as autoridades querem mais tempo para avaliar a situação. Rubio disse no sábado que o presidente levará até 60 dias para avaliar o impacto econômico das sanções e tarifas relacionadas à Rússia, das quais ele dispensou a aplicação no dia anterior. “Muitos de vocês ainda não sabem qual é a minha decisão, mas vamos descobrir, e vocês também vão descobrir”, disse Trump aos repórteres em seu clube Mar-a-Lago, em Palm Beach, na Flórida. A suspensão ocorre poucas semanas antes das eleições de meio de mandato de novembro, com Trump sob pressão devido aos preços altos de energia, à medida que a guerra com o Irã desestabiliza o abastecimento global de petróleo. Trump assinou na sexta-feira uma decreto suspendendo sanções e tarifas importantes previstas na lei conhecida como Lei Graham, que ele havia sancionado no mês passado a pedido de parlamentares que querem pressionar Moscou por causa da guerra na Ucrânia. As medidas, incluindo tarifas sobre produtos russos e penalidades para países que compram petróleo e gás da Rússia, deveriam entrar em vigor na próxima semana. O decreto de sexta-feira não especificou por quanto tempo a isenção duraria, mas Rubio disse que Trump optou por um período de revisão de 60 dias. “Acho que o presidente quer aproveitar esse período de 60 dias para, de certa forma, analisar o que a imposição tanto de sanções quanto de tarifas significará para a economia global e até mesmo para a economia dos Estados Unidos”, disse Rubio a repórteres antes de embarcar em um avião para uma viagem ao Uzbequistão. Para complicar ainda mais a situação, a Lei Graham prevê não apenas sanções contra a Rússia, mas também tarifas sobre produtos provenientes de países que importam suprimentos energéticos russos. Rubio citou a Índia, um importante parceiro dos Estados Unidos que diversificou seus suprimentos energéticos, mas continua fortemente dependente do petróleo russo. O decreto de sexta-feira [USN:L1N463009 TEXT:"gerou críticas"] do presidente ucraniano Volodymyr Zelenskiy, que alertou que ele encorajaria o presidente russo Vladimir Putin e prolongaria a guerra. FORNECIMENTO DE DIESEL Rubio também defendeu um acordo separado dos Estados Unidos com a Rússia para aumentar o fornecimento de diesel aos mercados globais, com o objetivo de amenizar os preços dos combustíveis, que subiram em meio à guerra com o Irã e às interrupções no abastecimento de energia. Segundo o acordo, Trump disse que a Rússia forneceria inicialmente mais de 300 mil toneladas de diesel aos Estados Unidos, seguidas por remessas em novembro e nos meses seguintes. “Esse diesel vai ser vendido de uma forma ou de outra”, disse Rubio. “A única diferença é a quantidade que os Estados Unidos iriam receber.” Rubio afirmou que o acordo sobre o diesel e a isenção das sanções refletiam o desafio de lidar com os conflitos no Oriente Médio e na Ucrânia, que têm prejudicado o abastecimento global de energia. “Esses conflitos ao redor do mundo estão começando a se sobrepor”, disse ele. (Reportagem de Nandita Bose, no Kentucky, e Gram Slattery, em Washington)

item.title: Zelenskiy says he spoke to US envoys Witkoff, Kushner
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Sunday he had spoken with US peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner as part of "virtually nonstop communication" between the two countries' teams aimed at the "next steps in diplomacy".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Sunday he had spoken with US peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner as part of "virtually nonstop communication" between the two countries' teams aimed at the "next steps in diplomacy". "Had a conversation with the American President's envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Peace comes only through strength and cooperation built on trust," he wrote on X. "In particular, we discussed the results of our teams' meeting in Florida. Our teams maintain virtually nonstop communication. We are also preparing the next steps in diplomacy."

item.title: Trump endorses Netanyahu in close Israeli election
item.description: The endorsement is not certain to give Netanyahu and his right-wing Likud party a boost in the October 27 national election.
item.dc:creator: Doina Chiacu, Alexander Cornwell
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump on Sunday endorsed his ally Benjamin Netanyahu as the longtime Israeli prime minister struggles for an edge in next week's parliamentary election. Trump praised Netanyahu as a "great warrior prime minister" and peace partner, crediting him with joining the United States in launching strikes on Iran in February. The conflict, in its seventh month, has disrupted energy markets globally and wreaked havoc across the Middle East, damaging critical infrastructure and destabilizing regional economies. "Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself," Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social. "Despite all of that, he has endured and, in fact, he has thrived! I have watched Bibi under the most trying of times. Normal men or women in such situations would have wilted under the pressure — But Bibi did not wilt, he actually got stronger, and maintains that same Strength today." In his message, addressed to "the Great People of Israel," Trump added, "Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu in his upcoming Race for Re-Election as Prime Minister of Israel." The Trump endorsement is not certain to give Netanyahu and his right-wing Likud party a boost in the October 27 national election, as Israeli public support for Trump has diminished amid Israeli-US disagreements over Iran. Polls have suggested no candidate has a clear path to power. Israel's prime minister is chosen through coalition-building in parliament rather than by direct popular vote. It will be Israel's first vote since the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023, that shook the country and plunged the Middle East into turmoil, as Israel went to war in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. The election could determine whether Netanyahu remains in power after one of the most consequential periods in Israel’s history, or is defeated by centrist rivals promising to usher in a new era. Netanyahu promptly expressed his thanks to his "dear friend Donald" on X, saying, "Together we will complete the mission!" Trump has broken with longtime US tradition by endorsing candidates in elections in foreign countries including Hungary, Colombia, Argentina, Japan and Honduras. ENDORSEMENT MIGHT HELP, CAN'T HURT Trump's relationship with Netanyahu has been close but also fractious, with the president at times publicly and privately criticizing Israel's longest-serving prime minister. The war that the US and Israel launched against Iran is unpopular with Americans, who vote November 3 in congressional elections, while support for Israel among Americans has also decreased over the Iran war and Israel's conduct in the three-year war in Gaza that Trump has promised to end. Both leaders on Sunday mentioned finishing the job in Iran. Tamar Hermann, a senior research fellow at the non-partisan Israel Democracy Institute in Jerusalem, said Trump's late endorsement could help win back wavering Netanyahu voters but was unlikely to draw widespread support. Most Israelis, even those who are critical of Netanyahu and his government, were largely in favor of the Iran war. In an election this close, "it couldn't hurt him, and it might help," said analyst Aaron David Miller of the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace in Washington. Netanyahu's religious-nationalist coalition is projected to lose its governing majority, although the opposition may also struggle to form a government, opinion polls show. That could lead to Netanyahu serving as a caretaker prime minister while another election is held. The US president passed up earlier opportunities to endorse Netanyahu, perhaps because he wanted to see what leverage he could exercise on issues like Gaza or Lebanon, said Miller. In the end, he said, Trump sided with a leader he sees as strong and unfairly persecuted. "However angry Trump may be at Netanyahu for pushing this Iran war, this in the end was a Trump decision," Miller added. A Trump decision not to endorse Netanyahu would have raised "legitimate questions about whether or not the whole Iran venture was in fact something Trump should have done," he said.

item.title: Lithuania says attempted Starlink arson was Russia-linked sabotage
item.description: Lithuania is treating an attempted arson attack at a SpaceX Starlink base station on Sunday as a Russia-linked act of sabotage aimed at undermining Ukraine's military capacity, the head of the government's National Crisis Management Centre said.
item.dc:creator: Andrius Sytas
item.content:encoded: Lithuania is treating an attempted arson attack at a SpaceX (SPCX.O) Starlink base station on Sunday as a Russia-linked act of sabotage aimed at undermining Ukraine's military capacity, the head of the government's National Crisis Management Centre said. Lithuanian authorities are searching for suspects who attempted to set fire to a Starlink base station on the outskirts of the capital Vilnius at about 2 a.m. (2300 GMT on Saturday), said Vilmantas Vitkauskas. The blaze was quickly extinguished, causing only minor property damage and no disruption to operations, he added. "We understand that this was not a routine arson attack but an act of sabotage," Vitkauskas told reporters in Vilnius. He said the incident was linked to earlier arson attacks against Starlink stations in Bulgaria and Poland. "They are part of Russian attempts to disrupt Starlink and influence the success of Ukrainian operations," he said. "Ukraine is the target." Ukraine uses Starlink terminals extensively for battlefield communications and installs Starlink receivers in many of its drones as part of their guidance systems. The [USN:L8N4600M6 TEXT:"terminals are used"] to conduct strikes on Russian targets inside Ukraine and help its interceptor drones defend against Russian drone attacks. Bulgarian authorities said fire was set to several Starlink antennas in the country on October 10, according to local media reports. And a fire at a Starlink facility in Poland in September damaged its power system and backup generator. Poland [USN:L1N45G0AS TEXT:"said at the time"] it believed the fire was an act of sabotage aimed at disrupting internet services, including for Ukraine's military, and blamed Russia. Four suspects [USN:L8N45Z0DS TEXT:"were detained"]. Moscow says such accusations are baseless and the result of anti-Russian hysteria.

item.title: Huracán Trudy azota costa del Pacífico mexicano, se espera se debilite esta noche
item.description: El huracán Trudy provocó fuertes lluvias y vientos intensos en algunas zonas del suroeste y centro-oeste de México a primera hora del domingo, mientras mantenía su fuerza y se desplazaba paralelamente hacia la costa del Pacífico.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El huracán Trudy provocó fuertes lluvias y vientos intensos en algunas zonas del suroeste y centro-oeste de México a primera hora del domingo, mientras mantenía su fuerza y se desplazaba paralelamente hacia la costa del Pacífico. El Centro Nacional de Huracanes de Estados Unidos (NHC, por su sigla en inglés) informó que Trudy se encontraba a unos 240 kilómetros al oeste de Manzanillo, con vientos máximos sostenidos de 165 kilómetros por hora (km/h). "Se prevén pocos cambios en su intensidad esta mañana, pero se pronostica que comenzará un rápido debilitamiento esta noche", dijo el NHC en su reporte más reciente. El ciclón se desplazaba hacia el noroeste, a unos 17 km/h y se prevé que permanezca cerca de la costa hasta el domingo por la noche, antes de debilitarse y desplazarse hacia el sur de Baja California Sur el lunes y el martes. Se espera que Trudy descargue lluvias de entre 10 a 20 centímetros a lo largo y cerca de la costa de Colima, Jalisco y Michoacán, lo que aumentará el riesgo de inundaciones y deslizamientos de tierra que podrían poner en peligro la vida, especialmente en terrenos escarpados. El Sistema de Alerta Temprana para Ciclones Tropicales de México (SIAT-CT) mantenía en alerta preventiva a 143 municipios de los estados afectados, incluyendo a Nayarit, también sobre la costa del Pacífico donde podrían registrarse oleajes de dos hasta seis metros de altura. En las últimas semanas, la costa del Pacífico mexicano ha sido golpeada por los huracanes [USN:L6N45L0YK TEXT:"Polo y Simon"], y la tormenta Rachel. Debido a las inundaciones, al menos ocho personas perdieron la vida en la ciudad costera de Ensenada, en el estado Baja California.

item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

FAST

Egypt is ready to provide Saudi Arabia with the support it needs to defend its security and stability, the presidency said on Sunday (Oct 18), as Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis intensify their attacks on the world's largest oil exporter. Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi requested an urgent parliament session to authorise the military, one of the Arab world's largest, to help defend Saudi Arabia if the kingdom requested its support. A parliamentary vote had been expected on authorizing the request for military support on Sunday, but discussions were due to continue on Monday, two lawmakers and local media reports said. HOUTHIS RAMP UP ATTACKS ON SAUDI ARABIA The Houthis have in recent days attacked Riyadh's international airport and the state oil giant Saudi Aramco, amid renewed fighting with the Saudi-backed forces of the internationally recognised government following the collapse of a truce.

"Egypt will provide Saudi Arabia with all necessary and possible forms of support to defend its security and stability, protect its resources, territorial integrity and Islamic holy sites," the Egyptian presidency said in a statement. It followed a meeting of Egypt's National Defence Council chaired by Sisi and attended by the parliamentary speaker, the prime minister and the army chief. Sisi said in a speech on Saturday that Egypt would act in accordance with guidance from Saudi King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed Salman, who visited Sisi on Sep 15, after fighting in Yemen reignited. Egypt and Saudi Arabia are close strategic and economic partners. Saudi Arabia and other oil-rich Gulf states provided Egypt with billions of dollars in aid, central-bank deposits and investments after the military ouster of President Mohamed Morsi in 2013. Egypt had previously joined the Saudi-led coalition that intervened in Yemen in 2015 to support the government against the Houthis, but played a limited combat role.

item.title: US resumes intelligence-sharing with Ukraine after pause, Zelenskiy says
item.description: Speaking to NBC's Meet the Press, Zelenskiy said intelligence-sharing was interrupted and later "de-blocked."
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The United States has resumed providing Ukraine critical intelligence to help it defend against Russian missile strikes, after a brief pause, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said in comments published on Sunday. Ukraine has relied on US intelligence to spot the fast-moving ballistic missiles that Russia has fired in waves at its cities. US President Donald Trump had [USN:L1N45Z16F TEXT:"said earlier this week"] that Washington was still sharing intelligence, although Ukrainian officials said some Russian strikes had occurred without warning. Speaking to NBC's Meet the Press, Zelenskiy said intelligence-sharing had been interrupted but later "de-blocked." "We are very thankful for this," he said. "Now it works." But Zelenskiy said other US actions, such as signing a deal to import Russian diesel and [USN:L6N464042 TEXT:"waiving sanctions on Russia"] that had been slated to take effect this week, will hurt Ukraine. "If the United States will officially take the side of Russia, of course if these two countries will be together, of course we will not prevail and we will not be able to stand," he said. Over the past week, a [USN:L6N46303A TEXT:"widening rift"] between Trump and Zelenskiy has sparked concerns that their tumultuous relationship could lead to even worse outcomes for Kyiv. Zelenskiy told NBC that he hopes Trump will remain an ally of Ukraine. "We want to trust him, and I hope that he will change his decisions," Zelenskiy said. "Because I think that it's all mistakes and it will not help us. And it will not help United States." In a Truth Social post on Sunday afternoon, Trump wrote that his decision-making was aimed at avoiding anything "that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table." Ukraine gets US help that Russia does not receive, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told NBC, citing intelligence-sharing and the provision of US munitions to other countries for resale to Ukraine. But Bessent, speaking with "Meet the Press" after it aired Zelenskiy's interview, did not directly answer when asked multiple times whether the United States views Ukraine as an ally. "Zelenskiy presents a false binary this morning that Ukraine must win," Bessent said. "The war must end, and that will be with some kind of a negotiated settlement."

item.title: Macron llama a la calma mientras Francia evalúa consecuencias de peores disturbios en últimos años
item.description: El presidente Emmanuel Macron hizo un llamado a la calma el domingo, un día después de que Francia viviera uno de sus peores días de disturbios en años, con miles de detenidos y tiendas saqueadas o dañadas tras las protestas por los altos precios y el deterioro de los servicios públicos.
item.dc:creator: Sybille de La Hamaide
item.content:encoded: El presidente Emmanuel Macron hizo un llamado a la calma el domingo, un día después de que Francia viviera uno de sus peores días de disturbios en años, con miles de detenidos y tiendas saqueadas o dañadas tras las protestas por los altos precios y el deterioro de los servicios públicos. Se produjeron nuevos enfrentamientos en París y Marsella, donde la policía antidisturbios intervino para impedir los intentos de saqueo de comercios. Las manifestaciones a nivel nacional se habían convertido en disturbios el sábado, con un ayuntamiento incendiado, tiendas saqueadas y edificios cubiertos de grafitis, mientras grupos violentos se enfrentaban a la policía en ciudades de todo el país. "Al ver estas imágenes, todos nos hemos preguntado: ¿qué les pasaba por la cabeza? ¿Cómo pueden los franceses hacerle esto a Francia?", declaró Macron en un discurso televisado dirigido a la nación. "Nada lo justifica, nada lo explica, nada lo excusa. Esta noche, todos sentimos ira y vergüenza". Los disturbios del sábado pusieron de manifiesto la profunda ira hacia Macron, que dejará el cargo en 2027 tras una década en el poder que se ha caracterizado cada vez más por el descontento social, una economía débil y una deuda galopante. Macron afirmó que quienes protestaban pacíficamente tenían motivos legítimos de queja y que sus acciones no debían confundirse con las de quienes buscaban sembrar el caos. No llegó a declarar el estado de emergencia, tal y como exigían algunos políticos de derecha, pero afirmó que el Gobierno tomaría medidas para permitir a los prefectos prohibir las manifestaciones si fuera necesario para proteger los edificios públicos y los comercios locales. LAS MANIFESTACIONES EN PARÍS, "COMO UNA ZONA DE GUERRA" El Gobierno ha achacado la violencia a lo que, según afirma, son grupos de extrema izquierda, así como a delincuentes que, según afirma, habrían instigado los saqueos. Un manifestante falleció el sábado tras sufrir un paro cardíaco durante las manifestaciones en París. La policía llevó a cabo 2.400 detenciones en toda Francia, mientras que casi 1.000 agentes resultaron heridos, según informó el ministro del Interior francés, Laurent Núñez. La policía volvió a enfrentarse a los manifestantes y lanzó gases lacrimógenos en la Place de la République el domingo por la tarde, mientras los manifestantes prendían fuego a montones de bicicletas. Un testigo de Reuters afirmó que parecía haber varios cientos de manifestantes en la zona. Se llevó a cabo una operación de limpieza a gran escala en ciudades desde Lille, en el norte, hasta Marsella, en el sur, y desde Estrasburgo, en el este, hasta Burdeos, en el suroeste, donde una turba enmascarada irrumpió en la residencia del prefecto local. «¡Esto parece una zona de guerra!», exclamó el empresario neerlandés Tije De Boer, que visitaba París con sus hijos y afirmó que los disturbios le obligaron a evacuar su hotel en la Place de la République. Más de medio millón de personas se sumaron el sábado a las marchas en decenas de ciudades, lo que supuso la convergencia de un movimiento estudiantil que lleva un mes en marcha con un descontento social más amplio contra el aumento del coste de la vida y el deterioro de los servicios públicos. VARIOS CIENTOS DE TIENDAS DAÑADAS Mientras cientos de miles de personas se manifestaban pacíficamente por toda Francia el sábado, grupos marginales violentos atacaron edificios públicos, saquearon boutiques de lujo y supermercados, y atacaron vehículos y agentes de policía. La líder de extrema derecha del Agrupación Nacional, Marine Le Pen, favorita de cara a la campaña presidencial del año que viene, también hizo un llamamiento a la calma, afirmando que Francia no debe acostumbrarse a las imágenes de un país maltratado, abusado y saqueado. "La violencia no es una opinión. La destrucción no es una forma de expresión. Y el caos no puede servir de proyecto para Francia", afirmó en un discurso grabado en vídeo. El candidato presidencial de extrema izquierda de "Francia Indómita", Jean-Luc Mélenchon, señaló que Macron debía dar respuesta a las reivindicaciones de los estudiantes de secundaria que se manifestaban. En Limoges, famosa por su porcelana, el derrumbe de la torre del reloj del ayuntamiento en medio de un intenso incendio reavivó los recuerdos del incendio de 2019 que devastó la catedral de Notre Dame de París. El alcalde, Guillaume Guerin, señaló que no se habían desplegado suficientes agentes de la policía nacional en su ciudad. "Hubo una clara intención premeditada de incendiar el ayuntamiento, y las personas que se encontraban en su interior temían por sus vidas", declaró Guerin a Reuters el domingo. Amenazó con dimitir si la ciudad no recibía los fondos necesarios para reparar el ayuntamiento. El ministro de Economía, Roland Lescure, se comprometió el domingo a apoyar a los propietarios de negocios que sufrieron pérdidas. "Quienes causen daños pagarán, repararán los daños y rendirán cuentas por su intención de sembrar el caos", afirmó Lescure en un comunicado. El director general de la cadena minorista francesa Carrefour (CARR.PA) , Alexandre Bompard, declaró a la cadena francesa BFMTV que 50 de las tiendas de la empresa habían sufrido daños, incluidas 20 que fueron saqueadas, y que las pérdidas por los daños ascendían a decenas de millones de euros.

SEOUL, Oct 18 : Samsung Electronics will use TSMC's 3-nanometre process to produce base dies for Nvidia's next-generation custom high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips, the Seoul Economic Daily reported on Sunday. The move would mark the first time Samsung has worked with the Taiwanese contract chipmaker at the HBM manufacturing stage, according to the report. • Nvidia has asked Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron Technology to use TSMC's process for NVHBM base dies, and sixth-generation DRAM technology for its core dies, the newspaper said, citing industry sources. • NVHBM, unveiled in August, integrates Nvidia's custom memory controller into the base die and is aimed at standardising implementation across multiple memory suppliers, according to the company.

item.title: In France's Limoges, the fire-ravaged town hall rekindles memories of Notre Dame
item.description: The 19th-century neo-Renaissance building survived two world wars.
item.dc:creator: Clotaire Achi
item.content:encoded: Residents in Limoges recoiled in horror on Sunday at the city's fire-ravaged town hall, an ornate 19th century neo-Renaissance building which survived two world wars but was torched by a masked mob during the [USN:L1N46302B TEXT:"worst unrest"] to convulse France in years. Stunned onlookers had watched helplessly the previous evening as the blaze tore through the roof, felling the building's clock tower in scenes that revived haunting memories of the collapse of Notre Dame cathedral's spire in a 2019 fire. "It broke my heart. I saw Notre Dame all over again, except this time it was our town," said Francoise Faurie who witnessed the fire consume Limoges' town hall. Faurie's family had been due to celebrate her grand-daughter's baptism in the town hall in a month's time. "What kind of country are we living in? What are we leaving our children?" she said. "There's no reason to touch that building. You can have demands, you have the right to protest, but not the right to violence." EXTENSIVE DAMAGE The local prefect, Maurice Barate, said the roof had caved in onto lower floors, sparing only the west wing, and that large parts of the exterior had been destroyed. The destruction of the building, a listed monument that opened in 1883 and was inspired by Paris' city hall, was a "heritage catastrophe", he said. Its central clock tower and belfry towered 43 metres (141 feet) over the square below. "It's inadmissible to have burned down the town hall!" one local resident, Gilbert, said. "Those who did this need to be punished. They need to pay out of their own pocket, it's not for the state to pay." The town's shaken mayor, Guillaume Guerin, described how the local police force had quickly been overwhelmed by several hundred-strong mob who he said smashed windows and used a battering ram to break down the main door. "The logistics, the organisation, the premeditation behind yesterday’s attack on the town hall is something I find unbearable," he told reporters. Guerin said there had been insufficient police numbers to protect the building since officers from the national force had been deployed to the street protest. "I had no single national police officer to protect the town hall," the centre-right mayor continued. "This country is doing badly, this country is doing very badly, and it’s a small provincial mayor telling you so." Crowds gathered under blue skies as specialists surveyed the damage. Edith Lorcen, a retired nurse, expressed her shock at the malice of those behind the attack. "I'm disgusted. I'm hurting," Lorcen said. "But it does nothing to add hate on top of hate."

item.title: Davidovich Fokina overcomes Jodar to claim Shanghai crown
item.description: Alejandro Davidovich Fokina ended Rafael Jodar's dream run at the Shanghai Masters on Sunday, battling back to beat his fellow Spaniard 1-6 7-6(5) 6-4 and clinch the biggest title of his career.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Alejandro Davidovich Fokina ended Rafael Jodar's dream run at the Shanghai Masters on Sunday, battling back to beat his fellow Spaniard 1-6 7-6(5) 6-4 and clinch the biggest title of his career. The 25th-seeded Davidovich Fokina is set to climb 13 places to a career-high world number 13 when the rankings are released on Monday. Jodar, playing in his first Masters 1000 final and the youngest Shanghai finalist in tournament history, made a blistering start, broke for a 2-0 lead and again to take the opening set. Davidovich Fokina recovered from a break down in the second set and saved break points in three successive service games before edging a tight tiebreak to force a decider. The momentum swung decisively in Davidovich Fokina's favour when he broke the 12th-seeded Jodar twice and sealed victory in two hours and 27 minutes. "I have a blank mind," Davidovich Fokina said. "I don't know what to say and I don't know how I feel. Just a huge relief. "After the first set I had to keep trying, keep pushing. In the tiebreak, I believed in myself again. In the third set, maybe I had a bit more fitness physically." It the third ATP singles title of the 27-year-old's career, adding to his ATP 250 triumphs in Chengdu and Mallorca this season. The first meeting between the two Spaniards pitted one of the ATP Tour's rising talents against a player enjoying the best season of his career. The 20-year-old Jodar, who was ranked outside the world's top 900 little more than a year ago, strengthened his bid to qualify for the ATP Finals in Turin in his first full season on tour.

item.title: Albanian PM says protests pose threat to EU membership, not government
item.description: Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama on Sunday rejected calls to step down and said street protests, which continued for a sixth day, were a threat not to his government but to Albania's hopes of joining the European Union.
item.dc:creator: Fatos Bytyci
item.content:encoded: Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama on Sunday rejected calls to step down and said street protests, which continued for a sixth day, were a threat not to his government but to Albania's hopes of joining the European Union. Student-led demonstrations, fuelled by anger over perceived government corruption, a lack of jobs and poor education standards, have engulfed central Tirana and spread to other cities in the past week. Demonstrators demanding Rama's resignation have set fire to government buildings as well as banks, smashed shop windows and pulled up paving stones to throw at police. Violence erupted again on Sunday when thousands gathered outside the Education Ministry and hurled rocks at riot police who responded with tear gas, water cannon and [USN:L6N46303U TEXT:"rubber bullets"]. The unrest, which followed months of largely peaceful protests over the summer [USN:L6N42J18T TEXT:"against a luxury coastal development"] backed by US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, poses the biggest challenge yet to Rama, who has governed since 2013 and last year won a fourth term in office. "I am not being challenged, the government is not being challenged, a government majority or a winning party in the elections is not being challenged but a path is being challenged, a mission is being challenged," Rama said in a live address on Facebook. “Albanians need to think very clearly: Do they want this, do they want that, or do they want the EU?” EU CONDEMNS USE OF VIOLENCE IN PROTESTS Rama invited students to talks as excavators dug up and removed the paving outside his office in central Tirana before protests started on Sunday. "This will not absolutely stop the protesters. This is just made to remove any way of protection of the protesters from the police. This is just that," said Elton Prendi, 40, a Tirana resident. The European Commission [USN:FWN4630JL TEXT:"condemned "]the use of violence in Tirana and other cities and welcomed authorities' commitment to protect people's right to protest. Rama canceled a meeting with Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker in Vienna scheduled for Monday, the Austrian chancellery said. Corruption scandals have tarnished Albania's image over the years and analysts say the country is a hub for gangs seeking to launder money from drugs and weapons trafficking. However, Rama has said his government is tackling corruption as never before. Along with Montenegro, Albania is currently leading the posse of Balkan countries seeking to join the EU, and is aiming for entry by 2030. Rama blamed unspecified foreign interests for the protests and for what he said was an attempted drone attack at his office this week. "God knows what the consequences will be. There are no young people, no students, and no minors who would even think of implementing this plan. This is a foreign hand," he said. Police said 388 people had been charged with criminal offences during the demonstrations. Scores of police officers and protesters have been injured.

item.title: One killed, 15 injured in Ukrainian drone attack on St Petersburg and Leningrad region
item.description: Ukrainian drones struck oil facilities and logistics and data centers, local authorities said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: One person was killed and 15 were injured in a Ukrainian drone attack on oil facilities, logistics and data centres in Russia's St Petersburg and the Leningrad region, local authorities said on Sunday. St Petersburg's governor Alexander Beglov said fires had broken out at the St Petersburg oil terminal, an oil depot and industrial warehouses. Russian e-commerce company Ozon said that its logistics hub in St Petersburg was on fire and the internet company VK (VKCO.MM) said that its data centre in the Leningrad region had been attacked by drones, but services were available to users as normal. Ukrainian drone producer Fire Point said on Sunday that the Ukrainian military had struck a VK data centre near St Petersburg. Russian air defence units downed 1,015 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions overnight, the Russian Defence Ministry said. Russia is constantly responding to Ukrainian attacks with systematic, large-scale strikes, the TASS news agency reported on Sunday, citing Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov. "The Kyiv regime is resisting. But this cannot change the course of events," he said, answering a question about how Russia might respond to Kyiv's attack on St Petersburg.

item.title: IMF/World Bank meetings leave developing countries with more questions than answers
item.description: Last week's meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank yielded no new answers for the developing world to the questions posed by a spreading Middle East war, continuing war in Ukraine, rising debt payments and a potential AI bubble.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal, David Lawder
item.content:encoded: Last week's meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank yielded no new answers for the developing world to the questions posed by a spreading Middle East war, continuing war in Ukraine, rising debt payments and a potential AI bubble. Not for the first time, [USN:L1N46302K TEXT:"lower-income countries"] are being rocked by the spillover from the actions of wealthier nations: rising debt service costs, higher inflation and the risk of falling ever further behind economically thanks to the AI boom. What they got was the stock advice the global lenders always dish out: to shrink fiscal deficits and accelerate economic reforms to attract more private sector investment. Kristalina Georgieva, the first IMF chief from a developing nation - Bulgaria - said advanced economies were in fact the worst offenders on budget imbalances. She noted that developing countries' debt levels had actually fallen in recent years, only for surging bond yields elsewhere to drive up their borrowing costs. Average debt service payments there had more than doubled from a decade ago to 14% of government revenue, crowding out education, healthcare and other critical areas, she said. ADVANCED ECONOMIES FOCUSED ON THEIR OWN PROBLEMS At a panel on Saturday, Georgieva said many issues remained unresolved, especially around AI: "We are in a place where we have many more questions than we have answers. And my alert to everybody is: Do not fall for the guys that pretend they have the answers. They are tricking you." Josh Lipsky, vice president of international economics at the Atlantic Council think tank, said the meetings had flunked their opportunity to come up with guidance or ways to help. "It's hard to talk about the developing world when the advanced economies don't have their act together and are at risk of a fiscal crisis," he said. "And that's on top of political situations in many of these countries that makes development aid not a priority at the moment." Mauricio Cardenas, Colombia's former finance minister and now a research scholar at Columbia University's School of International and Public Affairs in New York, said many policymakers were left with a deep sense that "something really bad could happen" but no real roadmap to navigate the future. "The IMF and World Bank are not particularly well prepared for this new phase. They understand that something is going on, they bring in experts on AI," he said. "But in the end, there's no kind of specific, concrete advice on how to be prepared for something where you don't really understand how it's going to unfold." The geopolitical tensions that have roiled both institutions since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 - complicating concerted action - were also evident in Bangkok when nearly half the delegates at an [USN:L1N46301V TEXT:"IMF steering committee"] walked out when Russia's finance minister spoke. Houthi attacks on Riyadh airport delayed the arrival of the head of that committee, Saudi Finance Minister Mohammed Al-Jadaan, who had to travel overland to Qatar to catch a flight. And Bangkok itself was a stark reminder of the challenges facing developing countries, still partly under water after floods in September that caused almost $200 million in damage to Thailand's industrial sector. RISING INEQUALITY COULD RAISE COSTS IN LONG TERM Kate Pickett, a professor at the University of York, urged policymakers to focus on more inclusive growth rather than forcing developing countries into tough structural reforms. "If inequality increases, if poverty deepens, that will increase their costs in the long term," she said. "It's not enough to describe an economy as resilient. It's only resilient for the rich and the privileged.” Ayhan Kose, deputy chief economist at the World Bank, said the global economy had weathered its biggest energy shock - from the US-Israeli war on Iran - better than expected. But while a global recession had been avoided, he said growth outlooks in both developing and advanced economies were worse than before. Growth had already fallen off in half of advanced economies, while in developing countries as a whole, it had slowed significantly to around 3.6% from 4.4%. “People are really worried because resilience today is not a guarantee for resilience tomorrow," he said. "Now they are worried about what will be the next shock, because every six months, if not every three months, there is a new shock." While no specific initiatives were announced, he said the World Bank remained focused on helping developing countries prepare for advancements in AI, in part by mobilising more private capital, now at triple the levels of 2022. Yet it, too, has to contend with sharp drops in official development aid and persistent challenges in attracting foreign investment to developing countries. “The reality on the ground is the reality on the ground,” he said.
